title: R31 Amendment: Add 3-Day Early Price Signal to FinBERT PEAD Scoring
rationale: Hadlock, Roberts & Lee (FinNLP Workshop, ACL 2025) benchmarked FinBERT vs BART encoder-decoder for PEAD text classification. FinBERT wins: 57.6% accuracy (positive drift group), 58.3% (negative drift group). Key enhancement: incorporating a 3-day post-earnings price signal as an additional input to the text model significantly boosts performance. The intuition is that the first 3 days of market reaction partially reveals institutional interpretation of the earnings call — adding this signal lets the model distinguish 'market agreed with our text score' (stronger signal) vs 'market disagreed' (weaker/reversed signal). This is a clean, low-cost enhancement to R31's FinBERT approach.
content:
### FinNLP 2025 PEAD Enhancement — FinBERT + Early Price Signal (ACL Anthology 2025.finnlp-2.13)
- Paper: Hadlock, Roberts & Lee. 'Enhancing Post Earnings Announcement Drift Measurement with Large Language Models.' FinNLP Workshop, ACL 2025, Suzhou.
- Benchmark: FinBERT vs BART encoder-decoder for PEAD direction classification
- FinBERT wins: 57.6% accuracy (positive group), 58.3% (negative group) — financial domain pretraining captures PEAD narrative signals
- Key enhancement: adding 3-day post-earnings price signal as auxiliary input improves model. Market's early reaction provides additional signal about institutional interpretation of earnings call.
- R31 Amendment: After computing FinBERT text surprise score, incorporate 3-day cumulative return as a confirmation/contradiction signal
  → If FinBERT score is positive AND 3-day return > 0: strong long signal (both agree)
  → If FinBERT score is positive but 3-day return < 0: weak signal (market disagrees with text) — reduce position size 50% or skip
  → This 'confirmation window' approach potentially separates text-confirmed drift from reversed calls
